title: Architecture patterns, smart/dumb components, full mock
exp: Architecture questions test whether you think at the system level. Smart/dumb component pattern, feature-based folder structure, error boundaries, and the full 30-minute mock complete the Angular track. Use your Zintara and BMS migration experience as concrete examples.
pts: **Feature-based folder structure:** group by feature (users/, compliance/, auth/) not by type (components/, services/, pipes/) — scales better, easier to lazy-load, clearer ownership

**Smart (container) vs dumb (presentational) components:** smart = injects services, owns state, dispatches actions; dumb = receives data via @Input, emits events via @Output, no service deps, easily testable and reusable
**State lifting:** when two sibling components need the same state, lift it to their nearest common ancestor or to a shared store service

**Error boundaries:** Angular does not have React-style error boundaries; use global ErrorHandler (`{ provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: GlobalErrorHandler }`) + per-component try/catch in effect() or catchError in Observables
**SSR considerations:** avoid window/document in component code (use isPlatformBrowser()); use transferState to avoid double HTTP calls; defer browser-only components with @defer
**Component API design:** prefer specific @Input types over `any`; use `model<T>()` for two-way bindable state; prefer signals over EventEmitter for complex component APIs
**Barrel files (`index.ts`):** re-export public API of a feature module; consumers import from `features/users` not `features/users/components/user-list.component`
pr: Refactor a service-heavy smart component into a container + dumb component pair
Add a GlobalErrorHandler that logs to console and shows a notification

viz.note: Full mock: 30 minutes — 1 architecture question (design the Angular side of the compliance evidence viewer), 1 debugging question (component not updating — diagnose), 1 behavioral (architecture decision you'd make differently). Score: stated trade-offs explicitly, used real project examples, clear reasoning under 2 minutes per answer.

qa.q: What is the smart/dumb component pattern and why does it improve maintainability?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Smart (container) components inject services, own state, and pass data down. Dumb (presentational) components only receive @Input, emit @Output, and contain no business logic. Benefits: dumb components are reusable anywhere (no service dependencies), easily unit-tested (just pass @Input values and verify output), and naturally work with OnPush (all data comes from @Inputs/signals). Smart components contain the side effects and async logic in one place. The pattern also guides code organisation — keep business logic in stores/services, keep templates in dumb components.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Signals build a fine-grained reactive dependency graph. When a signal value changes, only dependent view nodes are scheduled for DOM updating.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Mutating signal values inside effects without untracked() causes infinite change detection loops and browser freeze.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide predictable synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require adapting existing RxJS-heavy codebases.

qa.q: Why is feature-based folder structure preferred over type-based?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Type-based (components/, services/, pipes/) groups files by what they are — a component for users and a component for orders live in the same folder. Feature-based (users/, orders/) groups files by what they belong to — all users files are together. Feature-based advantages: lazy loading maps 1:1 to features, team ownership is clearer (the users team owns the users folder), and when you add a user feature you touch one folder instead of five. Type-based creates coupling across features — a change to user logic touches components, services, pipes, and models in separate locations.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Angular compiler generates Ivy instructions, linking component templates to DOM nodes with change detection dirty checking.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing heavy computations inside template expressions runs on every change detection cycle, causing UI lag.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** OnPush change detection skips subtrees unless inputs change, drastically improving performance at the cost of strict immutability.

qa.q: How do you handle global errors in Angular without component-level try/catch?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Provide a custom ErrorHandler: { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: GlobalErrorHandler }. The handleError(error) method is called whenever an unhandled error occurs in any component, service, or effect. Use it to: show a notification toast, log to Sentry or other monitoring, navigate to an error page. For HTTP errors, an error interceptor is more appropriate (handles specific status codes). For Observable errors within components, use catchError in the pipe. The combination — global ErrorHandler + error interceptor + per-Observable catchError — covers most error scenarios.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Observables push events asynchronously over time. Operators (switchMap, mergeMap, concatMap) transform streams via push-based notifications.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Unsubscribed long-lived observables (e.g. interval, HTTP, Store) create severe memory leaks when components destroy.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** switchMap cancels previous pending requests ideal for search auto-complete, whereas mergeMap executes all concurrently.

qa.q: How would you walk through migrating a large Angular 12 NgModule app to modern Angular 22?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** 1) Upgrade Angular incrementally to v22. 2) Enable standalone component migration: run ng generate @angular/core:standalone with the mode=convert-to-standalone schematic. 3) Enable OnPush on all components. 4) Replace Observable-based shared state with signal services. 5) Replace @Input()/@Output() with input()/output() and model() for two-way. 6) Add provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection() and test. 7) Replace lazy NgModules with loadComponent/loadChildren. 8) Add @defer to below-fold heavy components. 9) Migrate tests from Karma to Vitest. Each step is independently deployable — you don't need to do it all at once.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Signals build a fine-grained reactive dependency graph. When a signal value changes, only dependent view nodes are scheduled for DOM updating.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Mutating signal values inside effects without untracked() causes infinite change detection loops and browser freeze.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide predictable synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require adapting existing RxJS-heavy codebases.

qa.q: What is a barrel file and what are the trade-offs of using it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A barrel file (usually index.ts) re-exports the public API of a feature: export { UserCardComponent } from './components/user-card.component'; export { UserStore } from './services/user.store'. Consumers import from 'features/users' instead of 'features/users/components/user-card.component'. Benefits: consumers are decoupled from internal file structure, refactoring internals doesn't break imports, clear public vs private API. Trade-offs: can cause circular dependency issues if not managed carefully, and some bundlers (Angular's esbuild) can slightly reduce tree-shaking effectiveness — mitigated by keeping barrels lean.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Indexes store data in B-Tree structures. Clustered indexes dictate physical row storage on disk leaf pages; non-clustered indexes point to clustered keys or RIDs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Over-indexing degrades write performance on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations and leads to index fragmentation and page splits.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Covering indexes eliminate costly Key Lookups for read-heavy workloads but increase storage footprint and write transaction overhead.

interviewPlaybook.openingScript: When building Angular client applications at scale, I design Architecture patterns, smart/dumb components, full mock around predictable state propagation and minimal DOM change detection overhead.
interviewPlaybook.incidentStory: Our analytics dashboard experienced noticeable UI frame drops (jank) during live data streaming due to unoptimized Architecture patterns, smart/dumb components, full mock. I refactored the component architecture to fine-grained reactivity, eliminated unnecessary change detection cycles, and restored solid 60 FPS rendering.
